text: All edge cases behave sensibly. Let me run doctests in the module itself and do a final full test run:

raw_message.reasoning:
All good. Note `_compare_by_keys` doesn't compare build metadata at all — that's pre-existing behavior (semver 2.8.1 ignores build in comparison). My tuple comparison inherits this, matching how VersionInfo-vs-VersionInfo behaves. So `V(1,2,3,'rc.1','b1') == V(1,2,3,'rc.1','b2')` → True (pre-existing). For tuples same. Consistent.

Now, one concern: `v != '1.2.3'` returns True (correct). `v == '1.2.3'` False.

Also check: `_nat_cmp` only compares on prerelease; build ignored. Fine.

Now let me also run the doctests (`python semver.py`) since `if __name__ == "__main__": doctest.testmod()`, to make sure the new docstrings pass. The `replace` docstring example: `semver.replace("1.2.3", major=2, minor=3)` → '2.3.3' ✓.

Run python semver.py -v? That runs doctest; let me run briefly.
